..
An area of surface convergence embedded within the monsoon trough and
a trailing surface trough from the north will bring wetter weather 
over the Marianas, particularly over Guam and Rota. Scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected this evening, 
increasing to numerous showers for Guam and Rota after midnight and 
continuing through Wednesday night. Locally heavy showers are 
possible during this time period, although, flash flood concerns are 
too low for any hydrology products at this time. So, opted for a 
headline for Guam and Rota to indicate the possibility for locally 
heavy rainfall and stronger gusts within those showers. Then, the 
monsoon trough will remain active near Guam and Rota through the rest
of the week, whereas Saipan and Tinian will see a reduction in winds
and shower coverage shortly after midweek. Looking towards the end 
of the week, models indicate a tropical disturbance potentially 
forming over the region or to the west. Due to disagreements between 
model solutions and a lack of any notable circulations on satellite, 
uncertainty is high regarding this pattern, so the weekend forecast 
tops out at 30 and 40 percent between the two zones. Finally, benign 
conditions are possible next week during the holiday.

Marine...
The only altimetry pass indicates combined seas of 6 to 8 ft far to
the west, so combined seas are forecast to be 5 to 7 over the region
and steadily decreasing as the northerly swell subsides. Then, a 
long-period northeasterly swell will approach the region after 
midweek, increasing combined seas by a foot or two over the weekend. 
Surf will be elevated along north facing reefs tonight before quickly
decreasing a few feet as the northerly swell retreats. Once the 
long-period northeasterly swells reaches the region after midweek, 
however, surf and rip current risks may become hazardous for north 
and east facing reefs. This situation will continue to be monitored, 
so those with marine interests should stay up to date with the 
forecast.

Tropical Systems...
At 100 PM, Tropical Storm Koguma (27W) was centered 315 miles north-
northwest of Kwajalein near 13N167E, moving northwest at 10 mph. 
Maximum sustained winds were 50 mph. TS Koguma is expected to make a
slow turn toward the west-northwest over the next couple of days as 
it slowly strengthens, possibly becoming a typhoon Wednesday night 
or Thursday. Koguma is not expected to directly impact the Marianas 
or Micronesia.

For more information on TS Koguma, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and from the 
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Weak convergence to the south of the monsoon trough will continue to
weaken through the afternoon and evening, with scattered showers and
isolated thunderstorms over Pohnpei and Kosrae becoming isolated 
showers near midnight. Afterwards, Pohnpei and Kosrae look to remain
dry through the weekend as the monsoon trough pulls a little farther
north with TS Koguma. For Majuro, a drier regime is currently in 
place and looks to continue through Thursday night, with increased 
showers and thunderstorms by the end of the week as the monsoon 
trough reorients farther south from Koguma. 

For the marine forecast, not much has changed. Winds have subsided,
as expected, at Majuro, allowing the Small Craft Advisory (SCA) to 
expire. Seas and winds will remain below SCA levels through the
remainder of the week and through the weekend. Seas look to drop to
around 3 to 4 feet for all locations for the weekend.

Western Micronesia...
The monsoon surge remains the dominant feature in the region. This
feature is currently located over Palau and Yap, and producing 
scattered to widespread showers with isolated thunderstorms, and 10 
to 15 mph (10 to 15 kt) with occasional gusts up to 30 mph (25 kt) 
Wednesday at Palau. QPF model guidance suggests about up to an inch
of rain per day is possible for both islands. Overall, a wet week is
to be expected with calmer winds.

Further to the east, Chuuk can expect a quite benign weather pattern
through the week as a ridge of high pressure has set up over the
region. 

Altimetry shows combined seas of 5 to 7 feet across the region, with
the highest to the east of Yap. Winds are expected to be gentle to 
moderate with gusts to strong for Palau and Yap, while winds near 
Chuuk is expected to be light to gentle. Overall, near the monsoon 
surge seas are expected to be elevated and choppy, then becoming 
more benign to the east. Seas near Palau and Yap are expected to 
gradually taper down by a foot by the beginning of next week. Seas 
near Chuuk are expected to remain steady through the weekend.
